G1100.strongs: the tongue; by implication, a language (specially, one naturally unacquired)
senses: a tongue, language: [[r:ACT.2.11|Act 2:11]]; joined with φυλή, λαός, ἔθνος, frequently in pl., [[r:REV.5.9|Rev 5:9 7:9 10:11 11:9 13:7 14:6 17:15]]; λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γ., [[r:ACT.2.4|Act 2:4]]; γ. λαλεῖν καιναῖς, WH, txt. (RV, mg., omit καιναῖς), [[r:MRK.16.17|Mrk 16:17]]; λαλεῖν γλώσσαις, γλώσσῃ (see ICC, ll. with; DB, iv, 793ff.), [[r:MRK.16.17|Mrk 16:17]], WH, txt., R, mg., [[r:ACT.10.46|Act 10:46 19:6]], [[r:1CO.12.30|1Co 12:30 13:1]] [[r:1COR.14.2|14:2]], 4-6, 13, 18, 23, 27, 39; γλῶσσαι (= λόγοι ἐν γλώσσῃ, [[r:1CO.14.19|1Co 14:19]]), [[r:1CO.13.8|1Co 13:8 14:22]]; γένη γλωσσῶν, [[r:1CO.12.10|1Co 12:10, 28]]; προσεύχεσθαι γλώσσῃ, [[r:1CO.14.14|1Co 14:14]]; γλῶσσαν ἔχειν, [[r:1CO.14.26|1Co 14:26]] (Cremer, 163, 679). † (AS)

G1101.forms: γλωσσόκομον, -ου, τό, vernac. form of cl. γλωσσοκομεῖον
G1101.strongs: properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially) purse
senses: = cl. -εῖον (see supr.), a case for holding the reeds or tongues of musical instruments.
As in LXX, π. (MM, see word), a box, chest: [[r:JHN.12.6|Jhn 12:6 13:29]]. † (AS)

G1102.forms: γναφεύς, -έως, ὁ, Ion. and κοινή form of Att. κναφεύς
G1102.root: by variation for a derivative from κνάπτω (to tease cloth)

senses: prop., lawfully begotten, born in wedlock (in π., γυνὴ γ., a lawful wife; MM, see word).
true, genuine, sincere: [[r:PHP.4.3|Php 4:3]], [[r:1TI.1.2|1Ti 1:2]], [[r:TIT.1.4|Tit 1:4]]; as subst., τὸ γ. = ἡ γνησιότης, sincerity, [[r:2CO.8.8|2Co 8:8.]] † (AS)
sincerely, honourably: [[r:PHP.2.20|Phi 2:20]] (for a parallel in π., see MM, see word).† (AS)
darkness, gloom (including "an element of tempest," Tr., Syn., §with): [[r:HEB.12.18|Heb 12:18.]]† SYN.: ἀχλύς, ζόφος, σκότος (Tr., l.with; DB, i, 457a). (AS)

G1106.strongs: cognition, i.e. (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively) resolve (counsel, consent, etc.)
G1106.kjv: advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will
senses: In Attic writers, the mind, its operations and results (see Edwards, Lex., App., A);
royal purpose, decree (as in Da, I and II Es): [[r:REV.17.17|Rev 17:17]] (Cremer, 671). † (AS)

G1107.strongs: to make known; subjectively, to know
G1107.kjv: certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot
senses: as most commonly in cl., to come to know, discover, know: [[r:PHP.1.22|Php 1:22]] (but cf. R, mg.).

to make known: with accusative, [[r:ROM.9.22|Rom 9:22, 23]]; with accusative of thing(s) da.t. of person(s), [[r:LUK.2.15|Luk 2:15]], [[r:JHN.15.15|Jhn 15:15 17:26]], [[r:ACT.2.28|Act 2:28]]" (LXX), [[r:1CO.15.1|1Co 15:1]], [[r:2CO.8.1|2Co 8:1]], [[r:GAL.1.11|Gal 1:11]], [[r:EPH.1.9|Eph 1:9 6:19, 21]] [[r:COL.4.7|Col 4:7]], 9 [[r:2PE.1.16|2Pe 1:16]]; with dative, before ὅτι, [[r:1CO.12.3|1Co 12:3]]; before τί, [[r:COL.1.27|Col 1:27]]; περί, [[r:LUK.2.17|Luk 2:17.]] Pass., [[r:ACT.7.13|Act 7:13]], [[r:ROM.16.26|Rom 16:26]], [[r:EPH.3.3|Eph 3:3]], 6 10, [[r:PHP.4.6|Php 4:6]] (Cremer, 677; cf. ἀνα-, δια-γνωρίζω). † (AS)

knowledge, in NT, specially of the kn. of spiritual truth: absol., [[r:LUK.11.52|Luk 11:52]], [[r:ROM.2.20|Rom 2:20 15:14]], [[r:1CO.1.5|1Co 1:5]] (Lft., Notes, 147) 8:1, 7, 10, 11, 13:2, 8 14:6, [[r:2CO.6.6|2Co 6:6 8:7 11:6]], [[r:EPH.3.19|Eph 3:19]], [[r:COL.2.3|Col 2:3]], [[r:1PE.3.7|1Pe 3:7]], [[r:2PE.1.5|2Pe 1:5]], 6; with genitive obj., σωτηρίας, [[r:LUK.1.77|Luk 1:77]]; τ. δόξης τ. θεοῦ, [[r:2CO.4.6|2Co 4:6]]; τ. θεοῦ, [[r:2CO.2.14|2Co 2:14 10:5]]; Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, [[r:PHP.3.8|Php 3:8]] (see Deiss., LAE, 383.8), [[r:2PE.3.18|2Pe 3:18]]; with genitive subjc., θεοῦ, [[r:ROM.11.33|Rom 11:33]]; λόγος γνώσεως, [[r:1CO.12.8|1Co 12:8]]; ψευδωνύμου γνώσεως, [[r:1TI.6.20|1Ti 6:20.]] † SYN.: σοφία, φρόνησις (cf. ἐπί-γνωσις and see Lft. on [[r:COL.2.3|Col 2:3]]; Cremer, 156). (AS)

γνωστός, -ή, -όν, later form of γνωστός (γιγνώσκω), known: [[r:ACT.9.42|Act 9:42]]; with dative, [[r:JHN.18.15|Jhn 18:15, 16]] (Rec.), [[r:ACT.1.19|Act 1:19 2:14 4:10 13:38 15:18 19:17 28:22, 28]]; γ. σημεῖον, a notable (EV) sign, one that is matter of knowledge, [[r:ACT.4.16|Act 4:16]]; γνωστὸν, [[r:ACT.15.17|Act 15:17, 18]]; τὸ γνωστὸν θεοῦ, [[r:ROM.1.19|Rom 1:19]]; in pl., as subst., γνωστοί, acquaintances, [[r:LUK.2.44|Luk 2:44 23:49]]; so in sing., [[r:JHN.18.16|Jhn 18:16]] (WH).† (AS)

to mutter, murmur: [[r:1CO.10.10|1Co 10:10]]; before κατά, [[r:MAT.20.11|Mat 20:11]]; πρός, [[r:LUK.5.30|Luk 5:30]]; περί, [[r:JHN.6.41|Jhn 6:41, 61]]; μετ᾽ ἀλλήλων, [[r:JHN.6.43|Jhn 6:43]]; with accusative, before περί, [[r:JHN.7.32|Jhn 7:32]] (cf. δια-γογγύζω).† (AS)
a murmuring, muttering: [[r:JHN.7.12|Jhn 7:12]], [[r:ACT.6.1|Act 6:1]]; ἄνευ γ., [[r:1PE.4.9|1Pe 4:9]]; pl., χωρὶς γ., [[r:PHP.2.14|Php 2:14.]]† (AS)

G1114.strongs: properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e. (by implication) an imposter

G1115.strongs: the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem
senses: Γολγοθά (Rec. -θᾶ; WH, mg., Γολγόθ, Jo, l.with, Aram. גָּלְגָּלְתָּא = Heb. גֻּלְגֹּלֶת, LXX, κρανίον, [[r:JDG.9.53|Jdg 9:53]], [[r:2SA.9.35|2Ki 9:35]]); indecl. (exc. [[r:MRK.15.22|Mrk 15:22]], -άν), Golgotha, the place of the crucifixion: [[r:MAT.27.33|Mat 27:33]], [[r:MRK.15.22|Mrk 15:22]], [[r:JHN.19.17|Jhn 19:17]].† (AS)

G1116.strongs: Gomorrha (i.e. Amorah), a place near the Dead Sea
senses: Gomorrah, one of the cities of the plain (Gen.19): [[r:MAT.10.15|Mat 10:15]], [[r:ROM.9.29|Rom 9:29]]" (LXX), [[r:2PE.2.6|2Pe 2:6]], Ju 7.† (AS)

G1117.strongs: a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by extension) wares

senses: (γίγνομαι), a begetter, a father; mostly in pl., οἱ γ., parents: [[r:LUK.2.41|Luk 2:41, 43 8:56 21:16]], [[r:JHN.9.2|Jhn 9:2, 3 20, 22, 23]] [[r:ROM.1.30|Rom 1:30]], [[r:2CO.12.14|2Co 12:14]], [[r:EPH.6.1|Eph 6:1]], [[r:COL.3.20|Col 3:20]], [[r:2TI.3.2|2Ti 3:2]]; accusative pl. (Hellenistic, see Thackeray, Gr., i, 148), γονεῖς, [[r:MAT.10.21|Mat 10:21]], [[r:MRK.13.22|Mrk 13:22]], [[r:LUK.2.27|Luk 2:27 18:29]], [[r:JHN.9.18|Jhn 9:18]].† (AS)

the knee: [[r:HEB.12.12|Heb 12:12]]; of a suppliant, προσπίπτειν τοῖς γ., [[r:LUK.5.8|Luk 5:8]]; so also τιθέναι τὰ γ., to kneel: [[r:LUK.22.41|Luk 22:41]], [[r:ACT.7.60|Act 7:60 9:40 20:36 21:5]]; in mockery, [[r:MRK.15.19|Mrk 15:19]]; κάμπτειν τὰ γ., to bend the knee: [[r:ROM.11.4|Rom 11:4]] (LXX) 14:11 (LXX), [[r:EPH.3.14|Eph 3:14]], [[r:PHP.2.10|Php 2:10]].† (AS)

G1120.root: from a compound of [[w:G1119]] and the alternate of [[w:G4098]]
senses: to fall on the knees: before ἔμπροσθεν, [[r:MAT.27.29|Mat 27:29.]]
to fall down before one: with accusative, [[r:MAT.17.14|Mat 17:14]], [[r:MRK.1.40|Mrk 1:40]], R, txt., 10:17. † (AS)

G1121.strongs: a writing, i.e. a letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural learning
G1121.kjv: bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written
senses: that which is traced or drawn, a picture.
that which is written; (1) a character, letter: [[r:GAL.6.11|Gal 6:11]]; (2) a writing, a written document;
a letter: [[r:ACT.28.21|Act 28:21]]; (with) τὰ ἱερὰ γ., the sacred writings, i.e. the OT: [[r:2TI.3.15|2Ti 3:15]] (so in Philo, Vit. Mos., iii, 39);

τὸ γ., the letter, the written word as an external authority in contrast with the direct influence of the Spirit as manifested in the new Covenant: [[r:ROM.2.27|Rom 2:27, 29 7:6]], [[r:2CO.3.6|2Co 3:6]], 7; (3) τὰ γ., letters, i.e. learning: [[r:JHN.7.15|Jhn 7:15]], [[r:ACT.26.24|Act 26:24]]. (In π. an illiterate person is very frequently referred to as γράμματα μ᾽̀ εἰδότης, and this "never means anything else than inability to write": MM, Exp., x; but see also Cremer, 166; DCG, i, 202; ii, 584.) † (AS)

G1122.root: from [[w:G1121]]. a writer, i.e. (professionally) scribe or secretary
senses: In π., of a military officer (Deiss., BS, 110f.). So [[r:JDG.5.14|Jdg 5:14]], [[r:2KI.25.19|4Ki.25:19]] (ספר), al.

a scribe, a biblical scholar, teacher of the law (so first in I [[r:EST.8.3|Est 8:3]], II [[r:EST.7.6|Est 7:6]]; in [[r:LUK.5.17|Luk 5:17]], νομοδιδάσκαλος; in [[r:LUK.10.25|Luk 10:25]], νομικός): [[r:MAT.7.29|Mat 7:29]], [[r:MRK.1.22|Mrk 1:22]], and frequently in Gosp. γ. καὶ ἀρχιερεῖς, [[r:MAT.2.4|Mat 2:4]], and al.; γ. κ. Φαρισαῖοι, [[r:MAT.5.20|Mat 5:20]], and al.; γ. μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τ. οὐρ., [[r:MAT.13.52|Mat 13:52]]; ποῦ σοφός; ποῦ γ., [[r:1CO.1.20|1Co 1:20]] (Cremer, 167; DB, iv, 420, 800). (AS)

G1124.strongs: a document, i.e. holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in it)
senses: that which is written, a writing: πᾶσα γ., [[r:2TI.3.16|2Ti 3:16]]; γ. ἅγιαι, [[r:ROM.1.2|Rom 1:2]]; προφητικαί, [[r:ROM.16.26|Rom 16:26]]; al αἱ γ. τ. προφητῶν, [[r:MAT.26.56|Mat 26:56]]; ἡ γ., αἱ γ., the sacred writings, the Scriptures (i.e. the OT; see Milligan, NTD, 205); in pl., when the sacred writings as a whole are meant, e.g. [[r:MAT.21.42|Mat 21:42 26:54]], [[r:JHN.5.39|Jhn 5:39]], [[r:ROM.15.4|Rom 15:4]]; in sing., when a particular passage is referred to, as in [[r:LUK.4.21|Luk 4:21]], [[r:JHN.19.24|Jhn 19:24]], [[r:ROM.4.3|Rom 4:3 9:17 10:11 11:2]], [[r:JAS.2.23|Jas 2:23]] (Cremer, 165; DCG, ii, 584). (AS)

G1125.strongs: to "grave", especially to write; figuratively, to describe
senses: to scrape, graze (Hom.), and later (Hdt.) to sketch, draw.
of forming or tracing letters on writing material: Jhn.8:, [[r:GAL.6.11|Gal 6:11]], [[r:2TH.3.17|2Th 3:17]];

to express in writing, commit to writing, record: [[r:LUK.1.63|Luk 1:63]], [[r:JHN.19.21|Jhn 19:21, 22]] [[r:REV.1.11|Rev 1:11, 19]] al.; of scripture as a standing authority (Deiss., BS, 112ff.), γέγραπται, it stands written (Luther), [[r:MAT.4.4|Mat 4:4]], [[r:MRK.7.6|Mrk 7:6]], [[r:LUK.4.8|Luk 4:8]], [[r:ROM.1.17|Rom 1:17]], [[r:1CO.1.31|1Co 1:31]], al.; id. before ἐν, [[r:MRK.1.2|Mrk 1:2]], [[r:ACT.1.20|Act 1:20]], al.; with accusative, to write of: [[r:JHN.1.46|Jhn 1:46]], [[r:ROM.10.5|Rom 10:5]]; before περί, [[r:MAT.26.24|Mat 26:24]], [[r:MRK.14.21|Mrk 14:21]], [[r:JHN.5.46|Jhn 5:46]]; al.; with dative (WM, §31, 4), [[r:LUK.18.31|Luk 18:31]]; id. before ἵνα (M, Pr., 207f.), [[r:MRK.12.19|Mrk 12:19]], [[r:LUK.20.28|Luk 20:28]]; κατὰ τ. γεγραμμένον, [[r:2CO.4.13|2Co 4:13]]; γεγραμμένον ἐστί, [[r:JHN.2.17|Jhn 2:17]]; ἐγράφη, [[r:ROM.4.24|Rom 4:24]]; ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ γεγραμμένα, [[r:JHN.12.16|Jhn 12:16]]; (with) of writing directions or information, with dative of person(s): [[r:ROM.15.15|Rom 15:15]], [[r:2CO.7.12|2Co 7:12]], al.;

of that which contains the record or message: βιβλίον, [[r:MRK.10.4|Mrk 10:4]], [[r:JHN.21.25|Jhn 21:25]], [[r:REV.5.1|Rev 5:1]]; τίτλον, [[r:JHN.19.19|Jhn 19:19]]; ἐπιστολήν, [[r:ACT.23.25|Act 23:25]]; ἐντολήν, [[r:MRK.10.5|Mrk 10:5]] (cf. ἀπο-, ἐγ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, προ-). (AS)

G1127.forms: γρηγορέω, -ῶ, = Attic ἐργήγορα, pf. of ἐγείρω, which see
G1127.strongs: to keep awake, i.e. watch (literally or figuratively)
senses: to be awake; metaphorically, of being alive, [[r:1TH.5.10|1Th 5:10.]]

G1128.strongs: to practise naked (in the games), i.e. train (figuratively)
senses: Generally, to exercise, train the body or mind: [[r:1TI.4.7|1Ti 4:7]], [[r:HEB.5.14|Heb 5:14 12:11]], [[r:2PE.2.14|2Pe 2:14]]. † (AS)

G1130.strongs: to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly clad
senses: γυμνιτεύω (Rec. γυμνητ-, V. Tdf., Pr., 81), to be naked or scantily clad: [[r:1CO.4.11|1Co 4:11]] (cf. ἐν ψύχει κ. γυμνότητι), [[r:2CO.11.27|2Co 11:27]]; γυμνοί, [[r:JAS.2.15|Jas 2:15.]] In κοινή writers, γ. also means to go light-armed.† (AS)

G1131.strongs: nude (absolute or relative, literal or figurative)
senses: naked, without clothing, and sometimes (as frequently in cl.) scantily or poorly clad ([[r:ISA.20.2|Isa 20:2]]ff., [[r:TOB.1.16|Tob 1:16]], [[r:2MA.11.12|2Ma 11:12]]): [[r:MAT.25.36|Mat 25:36, 38 43, 44]], [[r:MRK.14.52|Mrk 14:52]], [[r:JHN.21.7|Jhn 21:7]], [[r:ACT.19.16|Act 19:16]], [[r:JAS.2.15|Jas 2:15]], [[r:REV.3.17|Rev 3:17 16:15, 17:16]]; as subst., to γ., the naked body, [[r:MRK.14.51|Mrk 14:51.]] Metaphorical, of things exposed, [[r:HEB.4.13|Heb 4:13]]; of the soul without a body (Plat., Crat., with, 20, and cf. Deiss., LAE, 293), [[r:2CO.5.3|2Co 5:3]]; of seed, bare, [[r:1CO.15.37|1Co 15:37]] (Cremer, 168).† (AS)

a woman, married or unmarried: [[r:MAT.11.11|Mat 11:11 14:21]], al.; ὕπανδρος γ., [[r:ROM.7.2|Rom 7:2]]; γ. χήρα, [[r:LUK.4.26|Luk 4:26]]; in vocat., γύναι implies neither reproof nor severity, but is used frequently as a term of respect and endearment, [[r:MAT.15.28|Mat 15:28]], [[r:JHN.2.4|Jhn 2:4, 4:21 19:26]].

a wife: [[r:MAT.1.20|Mat 1:20]], [[r:1CO.7.3|1Co 7:3]], 4 al.; γ. ἀπολύειν, [[r:MRK.10.2|Mrk 10:2]], al.; γ. ἔχειν [[r:MRK.6.18|Mrk 6:18]]; γ. λαβεῖν, [[r:MRK.12.19|Mrk 12:19]]; γ. γαμεῖν, [[r:LUK.14.20|Luk 14:20.]]

G1136.strongs: Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist

senses: Δαυείδ (Rec. Δαβίδ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. דָּוִד), David, King of Israel: [[r:MAT.1.6|Mat 1:6; 12:3]], and al.; σκηνὴ Δ., [[r:ACT.15.16|Act 15:16]]; κλεὶς Δ., [[r:REV.3.7|Rev 3:7]]; θρόνος Δ., [[r:LUK.1.32|Luk 1:32]]; ῥίζα Δ., [[r:REV.5.5|Rev 5:5]]; βασιλεία Δ., [[r:MRK.11.10|Mrk 11:10]]; υἱὸς Δ., the Messiah (Ps. Sol., 17:23; for other reff. in Jewish lit., see Dalman, Words, 317), [[r:MAT.1.1|Mat 1:1 9:27]], and al.; ἐν Δ., i.e. the Psalter, [[r:HEB.4.7|Heb 4:7]] (AS)

G1139.strongs: to be exercised by a dæmon
G1139.kjv: have a (be vexed with, be possessed with) devil(-s)
senses: (in cl. also δαιμονάω; δαίμων), to be under the power of a δαίμων (δαιμόνιον, which see), to be possessed: [[r:MAT.15.22|Mat 15:22]]; elsewhere always ptcp., -ιζόμενος, -ισθείς: [[r:MAT.4.24|Mat 4:24; 8:16, 28, 33 9:32 12:22]], [[r:MRK.1.32|Mrk 1:32 15 16 18]], [[r:LUK.8.36|Luk 8:36]], [[r:JHN.10.21|Jhn 10:21]] (Cremer, 171).† (AS)

G1140.strongs: a dæmonic being; by extension a deity
senses: an inferior divinity, deity or demon (as in magical π, Deiss., BS, 281; MM, Exp., x): ξένα δ., [[r:ACT.17.18|Act 17:18.]]
(a) in OT, heathen deities, false gods (e.g. [[r:DEU.32.17|Deu 32:17]], Psa.95 (96):5);

in NT, evil spirits, demons: θύουσιν δαιμονίοις, [[r:1CO.10.20|1Co 10:20]]; διδασκαλίαι δαιμονίων, [[r:1TI.4.1|1Ti 4:1]]; προσκυνεῖν τὰ δ., [[r:REV.9.20|Rev 9:20]]; ἄρχων τῶν δ., [[r:MAT.9.34|Mat 9:34]]; especially (syn. with πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον) as operating upon and "possessing" (of. δαιμονίζομαι) men: [[r:MAT.11.18|Mat 11:18]], and al.; εἰσέρχεσθαι δ. εἰς..., [[r:LUK.8.30|Luk 8:30]]; δ. ἔχειν, [[r:LUK.4.33|Luk 4:33]]; δ. ἐκβάλλειν, [[r:MAT.7.22|Mat 7:22]] In the phrase πνεῦμα δαιμονίου ἀκαθάρτου, [[r:LUK.4.33|Luk 4:33]], the wider cl. usage (1. b) is recognised, ἀκ. being elsewhere in NT, the epithet of πν., and δ. = πν. ἀκ. (see ICC, in l; Cremer, 168) (AS)

G1142.strongs: a dæmon or supernatural spirit (of a bad nature)
senses: in cl. and NT = δαιμόνιον; a demon: [[r:MAT.8.31|Mat 8:31.]]† (AS)

G1143.root: a prolonged form of a primary root

senses: δάκρυον (poët. form δάκρυ), -ου, τό, a tear: [[r:MRK.9.24|Mrk 9:24]] (WH, txt., R, txt. omit), [[r:ACT.20.19|Act 20:19, 31]], [[r:2CO.2.4|2Co 2:4]], [[r:2TI.1.4|2Ti 1:4]], [[r:HEB.5.7|Heb 5:7 12:17]], [[r:REV.7.17|Rev 7:17 21:4]]; metaphorically, dative pl., δάκρυσι ([[r:LAM.2.11|La 2:11]], Thuc., vii, 75; Bl., § 9, 3), [[r:LUK.7.38|Luk 7:38, 44]].† (AS)

δακρύω to weep, shed tears: [[r:JHN.11.35|Jhn 11:35.]]† SYN.: κλαίω, of audible weeping, to cry; ὀδύρομαι, of grief expressed verbally, to lament; θρηνέω, of formal lamentation, to sing a dirge; ἀλαλάζω, to wail in Oriental fashion; στενάζω, of grief expressed by inarticulate sounds, to groan. (AS)
indecl., Dalmanutha, an unidentified place near the Sea of Galilee: [[r:MRK.8.10|Mrk 8:10]] (cf. Μαγαδάν).† (AS)
Dalmatia, a part of Illyria on E. coast of the Adriatic: [[r:2TI.4.10|2Ti 4:10.]]† (AS)

G1150.root: a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning

G1152.strongs: perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian woman

G1153.strongs: a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus

G1155.strongs: to loan on interest; reflexively, to borrow
senses: δανίζω (late form of cl. -είζω, Rec., Bl., § 3; Thackeray, Gr., 85f.) to lend money on interest: [[r:LUK.6.34|Luk 6:34, 35]]; mid., to borrow: [[r:MAT.5.42|Mat 5:42.]]† SYN.: κίχρημι (see: χράω), to lend in a friendly way. (AS)

G1156.strongs: probably akin to the base of; a loan
senses: δάνιον, -ου, τό (late form of δάνειον, Rec.; see: δανίζω), a loan: [[r:MAT.18.27|Mat 18:27.]]† (AS)
δανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (late form of -ειστής, Rec.; see: δανείζω), a money-lender: [[r:LUK.7.41|Luk 7:41.]]† (AS)

G1158.forms: Δανιήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. דָּנִיֵּאל, God is my Judge)

G1159.strongs: to expend, i.e. (in a good sense) to incur cost, or (in a bad one) to waste
senses: to spend, expend: with accusative, [[r:MRK.5.26|Mrk 5:26]]; before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), [[r:ACT.21.24|Act 21:24]]; ὑπέρ, [[r:2CO.12.15|2Co 12:15.]]
to consume, squander: [[r:LUK.15.14|Luk 15:14]]; ἐν τ. ἡδσναῖς (on the constr. with ἐν, see Hort, Mayor, in l.), [[r:JAS.4.3|Jas 4:3]] (cf. ἐκ-, προσ- δ.).† (AS)

G1161.forms: δέ (before vowels δ᾽; on the general neglect of the elision in NT, see WH, App., 146; Tdf., Pr., 96)
G1161.kjv: also, and, but, moreover, now (often unexpressed in English)
senses: copulative, but, in the next place, and, now (Abbott, JG, 104): [[r:MAT.1.2|Mat 1:2]]ff., [[r:2CO.6.15|2Co 6:15, 16]], [[r:2PE.1.5|2Pe 1:5-7]]; in repetition for emphasis, [[r:ROM.3.21|Rom 3:21, 22, 9:30]], [[r:1CO.2.6|1Co 2:6]], [[r:GAL.2.2|Gal 2:2]], [[r:PHP.2.8|Php 2:8]]; in transition to something new, [[r:MAT.1.18|Mat 1:18, 2:19]], [[r:LUK.13.1|Luk 13:1]], [[r:JHN.7.14|Jhn 7:14]], [[r:ACT.6.1|Act 6:1]], [[r:ROM.8.28|Rom 8:28]], [[r:1CO.7.1|1Co 7:1 8:1]], al.; in explanatory parenthesis or addition, [[r:JHN.3.19|Jhn 3:19]], [[r:ROM.5.8|Rom 5:8]], [[r:1CO.1.12|1Co 1:12]], [[r:EPH.2.4|Eph 2:4, 5:32]], al.; ὡς δέ, [[r:JHN.2.9|Jhn 2:9]]; καὶ... δέ, but also, [[r:MAT.10.18|Mat 10:18]], [[r:LUK.1.76|Luk 1:76]], [[r:JHN.6.51|Jhn 6:51]], [[r:ROM.11.23|Rom 11:23]], al.; καὶ ἐὰν δέ, yea even if, [[r:JHN.8.16|Jhn 8:16.]]

Adversative, but, on the other hand, prop., answering to a foregoing μέν (which see), and distinguishing a word or clause from one preceding (in NT most frequently without μέν; Bl., §77, 12): ἐὰν δέ, [[r:MAT.6.14|Mat 6:14, 23]], al.; ἐγὼ (σὺ, etc.) δέ, [[r:MAT.5.22|Mat 5:22, 6:6]], [[r:MRK.8.29|Mrk 8:29]], al.; ὁ δέ, αὐτὸς δέ, [[r:MRK.1.45|Mrk 1:45]], [[r:LUK.4.40|Luk 4:40]], al.; after a negation, [[r:MAT.6.19|Mat 6:19, 20]], [[r:ROM.3.4|Rom 3:4]], [[r:1TH.5.21|1Th 5:21]], al. (AS)

an asking, entreaty, supplica­tion; in NT always addressed to God: [[r:LUK.1.13|Luk 1:13]], [[r:2CO.1.11|2Co 1:11]], [[r:PHP.1.19|Php 1:19]], [[r:2TI.1.3|2Ti 1:3]], [[r:JAS.5.16|Jas 5:16]], [[r:1PE.3.12|1Pe 3:12]]" (LXX); with νηστεῖαι, [[r:LUK.2.37|Luk 2:37]]; προσυνχή, -αί, [[r:EPH.6.18|Eph 6:18]], [[r:PHP.4.6|Php 4:6]], [[r:1TI.2.1|1Ti 2:1 5:5]]; ἱκετηρίαι, [[r:HEB.5.7|Heb 5:7]]; προσκαρτέρησις, [[r:EPH.6.18|Eph 6:18]]; ἐντεύξεις, [[r:1TI.2.1|1Ti 2:1]]; δ. ποιεῖσθαι (Deiss., BS, 250), [[r:LUK.5.33|Luk 5:33]], [[r:PHP.1.4|Php 1:4]] (pl.), [[r:1TI.2.1|1Ti 2:1]]; before ὑπέρ, [[r:2CO.9.14|2Co 9:14]], [[r:PHP.1.4|Php 1:4]]; περί, [[r:EPH.6.18|Eph 6:18]]; πρός, [[r:ROM.10.1|Rom 10:1.]]† SYN.: προσευχή, used of prayer in general, while δ. gives prominence to the sense of need; on the other hand, δ. is used as well of requests from man to man, while π. is limited to prayer to God. ἔντευξις, in the π., is the regular word for petition to a superior (Deiss., BS, 250; cf. the Pauline ἐντυγχάνειν, to entreat). Cf. also εὐχή. ([[r:JAS.5.15|Jas 5:15]]), αἴτημα, ἱκετηρία (Tr., Syn., § li; Cremer, 73, 174, 684). (AS)

G1163.strongs: also deon deh-on'; neuter active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is (was, etc.) necessary (as binding)
G1163.kjv: behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be) need(-ful), ought, should
senses: δεῖ impersonal (δέω), one must, it is necessary: with inf., [[r:MAT.26.54|Mat 26:54]], [[r:MRK.13.7|Mrk 13:7]], [[r:ACT.5.29|Act 5:29]], al.; with accusative and inf., [[r:MAT.16.21|Mat 16:21]], [[r:MRK.8.31|Mrk 8:31]], [[r:JHN.3.7|Jhn 3:7]], [[r:ACT.25.10|Act 25:10]], al.; with ellipse of accusative, [[r:MAT.23.23|Mat 23:23]]; of accusative, and inf., [[r:MRK.13.14|Mrk 13:14]], [[r:ROM.1.27|Rom 1:27 8:26]]; οὐ (μὴ) δεῖ (non licet), ought not, must not: [[r:ACT.25.24|Act 25:24]], [[r:2TI.2.24|2Ti 2:24]]; impf., ἔδει, of necessity or obligation in past time regarding a past event (Bl., § 63, 4), [[r:MAT.18.33|Mat 18:33]], [[r:LUK.15.32|Luk 15:32]], [[r:JHN.4.4|Jhn 4:4]], [[r:ACT.27.21|Act 27:21]], al.; periphr., δέον ἐστίν (as in Attic, χρεών ἐστι = χρή, see: δέον), [[r:ACT.19.36|Act 19:36]]; id., with ellipse of ἐστίν, [[r:1PE.1.6|1Pe 1:6]] τὰ μὴ δέοντα (= ἃ οὐ δεῖ [[r:1TI.5.13|1Ti 5:13.]] SYN.: ὀφείλει, expressing moral obligation, as distinct from δεῖ, denoting logical necessity and χρή, a need which results from the fitness of things (see Tr., Syn., § cvii, 10; Westc. on [[r:HEB.2.1|Heb 2:1]], [[r:1JN.2.6|1Jn 2:6]]; Hort on [[r:JAS.3.10|Jas 3:10]]). (AS)
= cl. παράδ- (cf. ὑπόδ-, [[r:2PE.2.6|2Pe 2:6]]), an example (a warning): Ju 7.† (AS)
(δεῖγμα), a rare word (ICC, ll. with), to make a show of, to expose: [[r:MAT.1.19|Mat 1:19]] (Rec. παραδ-, which see), [[r:COL.2.15|Col 2:15.]]† (AS)

G1166.root: a prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning
senses: δείκνυμι, δεικνύω (see Bl., § 23, 1; Veitch, see word), to show, with accusative of thing(s) (of person(s)), dative of person(s);

(δειλός), cowardice, timidity (never in good sense): [[r:2TI.1.7|2Ti 1:7.]]† SYN.: φόβος, fear, in general, good or bad; εὐλάβεια (which see), apprehension generally, but chiefly pious fear, "that careful and watchful reverence which pays regard to every circumstance in that with which it has to deal" (cf. Tr., Syn., § x).† (AS)
(δειλία), = the more frequently ἀποδ-, to be cowardly, timid, fearful: [[r:JHN.14.27|Jhn 14:27.]]† (AS)

G1170.forms: δεῖνα, ὁ, ἡ, τό (genitive -νος, dative -νι, accusative -να)
G1170.root: probably from the same as [[w:G1171]] (through the idea of forgetting the name as fearful, i.e. strange)
G1170.strongs: so and so (when the person is not specified)
senses: such an one, a certain one, whom one cannot or will not name: [[r:MAT.26.18|Mat 26:18.]]† (AS)

G1171.root: adverb from a derivative of the same as [[w:G1169]]

G1172.strongs: to dine, i.e. take the principle (or evening) meal
senses: (δεῖπνον, which see), to take the chief meal of the day, to dine, to sup: [[r:LUK.17.8|Luk 17:8 22:20]] (WH, br., R, mg. omits), [[r:1CO.11.25|1Co 11:25]]; metaphorically, [[r:REV.3.20|Rev 3:20.]]† (AS)

G1173.strongs: dinner, i.e. the chief meal (usually in the evening)
senses: the chief meal of the day, dinner, supper: [[r:MAT.23.6|Mat 23:6]], [[r:MRK.12.39|Mrk 12:39]], [[r:LUK.14.17|Luk 14:17, 24 20:46]], [[r:JHN.13.2|Jhn 13:2, 4 21:20]], [[r:1CO.11.21|1Co 11:21]]; δ. ποιεῖν, [[r:MRK.6.21|Mrk 6:21]], [[r:LUK.14.12|Luk 14:12, 16]], [[r:JHN.12.2|Jhn 12:2]]; κυριακὸν (which see) δ., [[r:1CO.11.20|1Co 11:20]]; metaphorically (Dalman, Words, 118), δ. τ. γάμου τ. ἀρνίου, [[r:REV.19.9|Rev 19:9]]; δ. τ. μέγα τ. Θεοῦ, [[r:REV.19.17|Rev 19:17.]]† (AS)

G1174.root: the compound of a derivative of the base of [[w:G1169]] and [[w:G1142]]
senses: δεισι-δαίμων, -ον (δείδω, to fear; δαίμων, deity) reverent to the deity, religious; compar. -μονεστέρους (AV, too superstitious, R, txt., somewhat superstitious, a sense in wh. the word is sometimes used; cf. Field, Notes, 125), more religious, God fearing, than others, quite religious (Abbott, Essays, 105 ff.; Deiss., LAE, 285): [[r:ACT.17.22|Act 17:22.]]† SYN.: εὐσεβής (which see), θεοσεβής, θρῆσκος (Cremer, 681; DB, ext., 142 a). (AS)
ten: [[r:MAT.20.24|Mat 20:24]], al.; θλίψις ἡμερῶν δ., i.e. of brief duration: [[r:REV.2.10|Rev 2:10.]]† δεκα-οκτώ, T for δέκα ὀκτώ, eighteen: [[r:LUK.13.4|Luk 13:4.]]† (AS)
δεκα-πέντε late form of πεντεκαίδεκα, fifteen: [[r:JHN.11.18|Jhn 11:18]], [[r:ACT.27.5|Act 27:5]], WH, mg., ib. 28, [[r:GAL.1.18|Gal 1:18]].† (AS)

G1179.strongs: the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in Syria
senses: Δεκά-πολις, -εως, ὴ Decapolis, a region east of the Jordan con­taining ten cities: [[r:MAT.4.25|Mat 4:25]], [[r:MRK.5.20|Mrk 5:20 7:31]].† (AS)

= cl. τεσσαρεσκαίδεκα, more frequently in later Gk. than the older form and in MGr. (for thirteen and upwards) universal, fourteen: [[r:MAT.1.17|Mat 1:17]], [[r:2CO.12.2|2Co 12:2]], [[r:GAL.2.1|Gal 2:1]] (cf. τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατος).† (AS)

G1181.forms: δεκάτη, -ης, ἡ prop. fem. (sc. μέρος) of δέκατος, -η, -ον
G1181.strongs: a tenth, i.e. as a percentage or (technically) tithe
senses: a tenth part, a tithe: [[r:HEB.7.2|Heb 7:2, 4; 8, 9]] (for a curious inversion of the Biblical use, see MM, see word).† (AS)

G1183.strongs: to tithe, i.e. to give or take a tenth
senses: = cl. -τεύω (δεκάτη), to take tithe of: with accusative of person(s), [[r:HEB.7.6|Heb 7:6]]; pass. to pay tithe: [[r:HEB.7.9|Heb 7:9.]]† (AS)
(δέλεαρ, a bait), to allure by a bait: metaphorically, to allure, entice: with accusative, [[r:2PE.2.14|2Pe 2:14, 18]]; pass., [[r:JAS.1.14|Jas 1:14.]]† (AS)

G1187.strongs: a guardsman (as if taking the right) or light-armed soldier
senses: (δεξιός, λαμβάνω), a kind of soldier, prob. a spearman (Vg., lancearius) or slinger: [[r:ACT.23.23|Act 23:23.]]† δεξιο-βόλος, -ου, ὁ (δεξιός, βάλλω), one who throws with the right hand: L for δεξιολάβος, [[r:ACT.23.23|Act 23:23.]]† (AS)

G1188.strongs: the right side or (feminine) hand (as that which usually takes)
senses: the right: [[r:MAT.5.29|Mat 5:29]], [[r:JHN.18.10|Jhn 18:10]], al.; ὅπλα δ., weapons carried in the right hand, i.e. for offence, [[r:2CO.6.7|2Co 6:7]]; ἡ δ. χείρ, [[r:MAT.5.30|Mat 5:30]], [[r:LUK.6.6|Luk 6:6]], al.; ἡ δ. (sc. χείρ), [[r:MAT.6.3|Mat 6:3]], al.; ἐπὶ τὴν δ., in the right hand (R, txt., on R, mg.), [[r:REV.5.1|Rev 5:1]]; διδόναι τὴν δ., in friend­ship (Deiss., BS, 251), [[r:GAL.2.9|Gal 2:9]]; metaphorically of power, τῇ δ. αὐτοῦ, [[r:ACT.2.33|Act 2:33 5:31]]; τὰ δ., the right side, [[r:MRK.16.5|Mrk 16:5]]; ἐκ δεξιῶν, on the right hand, with genitive, [[r:MAT.25.33|Mat 25:33, 34]], [[r:MRK.15.27|Mrk 15:27]], [[r:LUK.1.11|Luk 1:11]], al.; of a place of honour in the Messianic Kingdom (cf. [[r:3KI.2.19|3Ki 2:19]], Psa.44(45):10), καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν, [[r:MAT.20.21|Mat 20:21]], [[r:MRK.10.37|Mrk 10:37]]; of the heavenly session of Christ, [[r:MAT.26.64|Mat 26:64]], [[r:MRK.14.62|Mrk 14:62]], [[r:HEB.1.13|Heb 1:13]] (Cremer, 172) (AS)

G1189.strongs: to beg (as binding oneself), i.e. petition
senses: (mid. of δέω, II, which see, as depon.) to want for oneself;

in general: absol., [[r:ACT.26.3|Act 26:3]], WH; with genitive of person(s), [[r:LUK.5.12|Luk 5:12; 8:28; 38]] (ἐδεῖτο; T, ἐδέετο, cf. Veitch, see word δέω) 9:38, [[r:ACT.8.34|Act 8:34; 21:39]], [[r:2CO.5.20|2Co 5:20]], [[r:GAL.4.12|Gal 4:12]]; before ἵνα, [[r:LUK.9.40|Luk 9:40]]; before τό, with inf., [[r:2CO.10.2|2Co 10:2]]; with genitive of person(s) and of thing(s), [[r:2CO.8.4|2Co 8:4]];

of prayer to God: absol., [[r:ACT.4.31|Act 4:31]]; before εἴ πως, [[r:ROM.1.10|Rom 1:10]]; ἵνα, [[r:LUK.21.36|Luk 21:36; 22:32]]; εἰς τό, [[r:1TH.3.10|1Th 3:10]]; ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τ. κύριον, ὅπως, [[r:ACT.8.24|Act 8:24]]; with genitive, τοῦ κυρίου, ὅπως, [[r:MAT.9.38|Mat 9:38]], [[r:LUK.10.2|Luk 10:2]]; τοῦ Θεοῦ, [[r:ACT.10.2|Act 10:2]]; before εἰ ἄρα, [[r:ACT.8.22|Act 8:22.]]† SYN.: αἰτέω, and cf. δέησις. (AS)

G1190.strongs: a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe

G1191.strongs: Derbe, a place in Asia Minor

senses: (δέρω), the skin, hide of beasts: ἐν αἰγίοις δ., [[r:HEB.11.37|Heb 11:37.]]† (AS)

G1194.strongs: properly, to flay, i.e. (by implication) to scourge, or (by analogy) to thrash
senses: (of. Eng. slang, hide) to beat, thrash: with accusative, [[r:MAT.21.35|Mat 21:35]], [[r:MRK.12.3|Mrk 12:3]], 5, [[r:LUK.20.10|Luk 20:10, 11 22:63]], [[r:JHN.18.23|Jhn 18:23]], [[r:ACT.5.40|Act 5:40 16:37 22:19]]; ὡς ἀέρα δέρων, [[r:1CO.9.26|1Co 9:26]]; εἰς πρόσωπου δ., [[r:2CO.11.20|2Co 11:20.]] Pass., [[r:MRK.13.9|Mrk 13:9]], [[r:LUK.12.47|Luk 12:47, 48]] (δαρήσεται πολλάς, ὀλίγας, Sc. πληγάς).† (AS)

G1195.strongs: to be a binder (captor), i.e. to enchain (a prisoner), to tie on (a load)

senses: (δέω), a bundle: δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας (D, Orig., omit εἰς, and Blass thinks original reading, δέσμας δέσμας; see Deiss., LAE, 125.4), [[r:MAT.13.30|Mat 13:30.]]† (AS)

G1199.strongs: a band, i.e. ligament (of the body) or shackle (of a prisoner); figuratively, an impediment or disability
senses: (δέω), a band, bond: metaphorically, [[r:LUK.13.16|Luk 13:16]]; ὁ δεσμὸς τ. γλώσσης, [[r:MRK.7.35|Mrk 7:35]] (for this expression in π., see Deiss., LAE, 306 ff.; of actual bonds, see Ruth., Gr., 9). Pl., δεσμοί, [[r:PHP.1.13|Php 1:13]]; δεσμά (as also in cl.), [[r:LUK.8.29|Luk 8:29]], [[r:ACT.16.26|Act 16:26 20:23]]; genitive, dative, [[r:ACT.23.29|Act 23:29 26:29, 31]], [[r:PHP.1.7|Php 1:7, 14, 17]], [[r:COL.4.18|Col 4:18]], [[r:2TI.2.9|2Ti 2:9]], Phm 10, [[r:HEB.11.36|Heb 11:36]], Ju 6; ἐν τοῖς δ. τοῦ εὐαγγελίου Phm 13.† (AS)
